jobs.description:
Company Description
Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America (HMGMA) is Hyundai Motor Group’s first dedicated full Electric Vehicle mass-production facility in the United States, supporting the company’s vision to become a leading provider of electrified mobility solutions. Located near Savannah, GA, this state-of-the-art smart factory features cutting-edge production technology and advanced manufacturing processes. HMGMA is part of a major investment in Georgia that focuses on innovation, sustainability, and high-quality EV production. The facility is actively building a diverse team of skilled professionals to help shape the future of mobility and support long-term growth in the region.
Role Description
The Environmental Health Safety Specialist is a full-time, on-site role based in Savannah, GA, supporting safe and compliant operations within HMGMA’s advanced EV manufacturing environment. This role is responsible for implementing and maintaining EHS programs, performing regular workplace inspections, and monitoring compliance with federal, state, and local regulations. Daily tasks include conducting risk assessments, investigating incidents, maintaining EHS documentation, and supporting corrective and preventive actions. The specialist will deliver safety training, coach team members on best practices, and collaborate with production, maintenance, and leadership teams to drive continuous improvement in environmental, health, and safety performance. This position also assists with reporting, audits, and sustainability initiatives to ensure a safe and environmentally responsible workplace.
Qualifications

Strong foundation in Environment Health and Safety (EHS), Health & Safety, and Occupational Health, with the ability to develop and implement effective EHS programs.
Experience in Workplace Safety and Safety Training, including conducting safety orientations, toolbox talks, and ongoing education for team members.
Knowledge of relevant OSHA, EPA, and state regulations; experience with risk assessments, incident investigations, and corrective action processes.
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Occupational Health and Safety, Engineering, or a related field; professional certifications (e.g., CSP, CIH, CHMM) are a plus.
Prior experience in manufacturing, automotive, or industrial environments, preferably in a high-tech or advanced production facility.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate across diverse teams and promote a safety-focused culture.
Proficiency with EHS management systems, incident reporting tools, and standard office software; ability to prepare clear reports and presentations.

Job Title:
Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) Specialist

Job Summary:

The EHS Specialist is responsible for developing, implementing, and monitoring workplace safety programs. This individual identifies hazardous conditions and practices, conducts thorough onsite inspections, and ensures the facility adheres to local, state, and federal regulations (such as OSHA). They will be responsible for manufacturer and warehouse oversite locations and support first shift and second shift operations. The goal is to foster a culture of safety where every employee returns home in the same condition they arrived.

Key Responsibilities:

Inspections and Audits: Conduct regular walkthroughs of facilities and job sites to identify potential fire, safety, or health hazards.
Compliance Management: Ensure all operations comply with 29 CFR 1910(General Industry) and /or 1926 (Construction) standards.
Incident Investigation: Lead the investigation of accidents, near-misses, and injuries. Determine root causes and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
Training and Education: Develop and deliver safety training modules for employees on topics such as PPE, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), Fall Protections, Hazard Communication, Respiratory protection and other relevant environmental and safety training.
Environmental Oversight: Manage waste disposal protocols; water discharge from facility, runoff, and well water requirements; and air emissions related to paint booth.
Industrial Hygiene: Monitor factors related to employee exposure to noise levels; air emission exposure from brazing, welding, and paint operations; lasers, and chemical exposure.
Reporting: Maintain required safety logs (e.g., OSHA 300 logs and prepare internal reports for management regarding safety metrics and KPIs.

Qualifications & Skills: Requirement

Education: Bachelor’s degree in occupational health and safety or related field

Certifications: GSP (Graduate Safety Professional, ASP (Associate Safety Professional), CSP (Certified Safety Professional)

Technical Knowledge: Deep understanding of OSHA, EPA, and NFPA regulations.

Soft Skills: Strong communication skills, ability to influence behavior, and attention to detail.

Experience: 2 – 5 years of experience in an industrial or construction safety role.

Job Title: Environmental Scientist (Staff Scientist)

Job Description

This Environmental Scientist (Staff Scientist) role focuses on designing, supervising, and executing complex laboratory and field studies that assess the behavior and persistence of chemicals in the environment. The position plays a key role in delivering high-quality, regulatory-compliant environmental fate and ecotoxicology data to a global clientele across agrochemicals, industrial chemicals, pharmaceuticals, biocides, and animal health products. You will act as a technical expert, provide guidance to colleagues and clients, and contribute to the development of procedures, methods, and reports that support global regulatory submissions.

Responsibilities

Design and supervise simple and complex experiments and procedures in accordance with all applicable regulatory requirements, including but not limited to DEA, EPA, FDA, FIFRA, and OECD guidelines.
Develop procedures and methods to solve technical problems and improve laboratory practices and workflows.
Serve as a technical expert for staff and external customers, providing scientific guidance and support on environmental fate and related studies.
Perform advanced troubleshooting of instrumentation and equipment to ensure accurate and reliable data generation.
Conduct studies to determine the persistence, distribution, and behavior of chemicals in various environmental matrices such as soil, water, and other media.
Perform complex data evaluations, interpret results, and ensure scientific integrity and accuracy in all analyses.
Review the work and data generated by other staff members to ensure compliance with quality standards and regulatory requirements.
Write complex technical reports, including study reports and standard operating procedures, that clearly document methods, results, and conclusions.
Serve as a primary business contact for clients on assigned projects, providing updates, clarifying technical issues, and ensuring customer satisfaction.
Work concurrently on multiple projects, effectively prioritizing tasks and managing timelines to meet project and regulatory deadlines.
Monitor and direct activities of other staff within your area of expertise, offering technical leadership and mentoring.
Potentially serve as Study Director on one or more projects, overseeing Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) compliance and ensuring that all work on assigned projects meets regulatory and internal quality standards.
Confer with scientists and colleagues to plan research, discuss findings, and prepare technical papers and reports.
Train staff on laboratory techniques, methods, and procedures necessary to complete environmental fate and related laboratory assignments.
Maintain accurate records, follow established protocols and company policies, and support continuous improvement of laboratory operations.

Essential Skills

Demonstrated experience working in a GLP-compliant laboratory environment, including adherence to regulatory standards such as DEA, EPA, FDA, FIFRA, and OECD.
Strong Expereince in environmental science, environmental fate studies, or closely related disciplines.
Proficiency in chemistry and analytical chemistry, including chemical testing and wet chemistry techniques.
Experience in environmental fate studies that evaluate the persistence and behavior of chemicals in environmental matrices.
Working knowledge of environmental compliance and environmental field practices, including soil sampling and remediation concepts.
Familiarity with laboratory operations, quality control procedures, and environmental engineering or environmental remediation principles.
Ability to perform advanced troubleshooting of scientific instrumentation and laboratory equipment.
Strong computer skills and the ability to use scientific software and data analysis tools effectively.
Excellent scientific and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and prioritize tasks.
Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to write complex technical reports and standard operating procedures.
High attention to detail and a commitment to data integrity and quality.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team, demonstrating self-motivation, adaptability, and a positive attitude.
Ability to learn new techniques, perform multiple tasks simultaneously, and maintain accurate and complete records.
Bachelors degree in a relevant field such as chemistry, biochemistry, biology, or another directly related discipline.
Minimum of five years of experience in an environmental fate laboratory with direct involvement in GLP studies.
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Masters degree in a relevant field such as chemistry, biochemistry, biology, environmental science, or related discipline.
At least three years of directly relevant experience in an environmental fate laboratory when combined with a Masters degree, as a substitute for the bachelors degree plus five years of experience.
Experience in microbiology, biology, toxicology, or related life science disciplines.
Expereince in environmental engineering, environmental remediation, or related environmental fields.
Experience with analytical chemistry and wet chemistry methods applied to environmental and chemical testing.
Familiarity with laboratory-based quality control systems and procedures.
Experience as a Study Director or in project management within a GLP laboratory environment.
Experience working with agrochemicals, industrial chemicals, pharmaceuticals, biocides, or animal health products in a testing or research setting.
Ability to collaborate with a global client base and provide clear technical explanations to non-specialist stakeholders.

Work Environment

This role operates in both laboratory and field environments, providing exposure to a wide range of environmental and analytical testing activities. You will work in a highly specialized laboratory recognized for high-tier ecotoxicology and environmental fate studies that support global regulatory requirements for agrochemicals, industrial chemicals, pharmaceuticals, biocides, and animal health products. The site is known for its long-tenured staff, with many team members having 1020 years of experience, creating a stable, collaborative, and knowledge-rich environment. The organization is part of a large international life sciences network with hundreds of laboratories worldwide, offering access to advanced technologies, diverse scientific expertise, and opportunities to contribute to complex, high-impact projects across food, environmental, pharmaceutical, genomics, forensics, and advanced material sciences testing. The standard schedule is full-time, Monday through Friday, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with overtime as needed to meet project and regulatory deadlines. Work involves typical laboratory attire and adherence to safety protocols, including the use of appropriate personal protective equipment in both lab and field settings.

jobs.title: Water Resources Project Manager
jobs.description:
What We're Looking For

Are you looking for a new, exciting opportunity? We are seeking a highly creative and motivated engineering project manager with experience in water resources to lead project design. While the primary focus will be on local and statewide projects with municipal clients and the DOT, the candidate will have the opportunity to support other disciplines and projects through our firmwide practice. Join our more than 110 years of experience and be part of why HNTB consistently ranks as a top design firm nationwide by Engineering News-Record (ENR).

At HNTB, you can create a career that is meaningful to you while building communities that matter to all of us. For more than a century, we have been delivering solutions for some of the largest, most complex infrastructure projects across the country. With our historic growth, it is an exciting time to join our team of employee-owners.

This opportunity entails being responsible for managing assigned project(s) throughout their full lifecycle including developing the scope and technical sections of proposal and procurement documents to participating in contract negotiations and overseeing the delivery of the project plan to successfully accomplish HNTB’s 4 for 4 performance: delivery of quality work, on time, on budget and to the client’s satisfaction on every project. This position proactively manages the budget, schedule, technical requirements, contractual obligations, and client communications in support of the project’s objectives. Provides high level technical tasks while managing and reviewing design related specifications, calculations, reports and plans. Coordinates with internal and external partners including cross-discipline and functional teams to address and problem solve design related issues or concerns. The Project Manager I – Engineering typically manages project team(s) for one or more strategic (<$1M) projects or may lead and/or work as a discipline lead on a mini-mega ($1M to <$5M) project management team.

What You'll Do

Responsible for development of the project scope and fee quotation and assists in the preparation of technical proposals and contracts in accordance with HNTB's Sophisticated Contracting Approach (SCA).
Serves as the primary client liaison and manages the project team to deliver the scope, schedule, and budgets to completion and to the client’s satisfaction. Assists with client project scoping and contract negotiations.
Performs technical discipline tasks including analysis, reports, design, specification, and production for assigned projects.
Implements the firm’s project delivery plan using HNTB's Sophisticated Delivery Approach (SDA) on each project. Leads the development and the execution of the project management plan. Supervises and mentors team to overall project objectives.
Performs coordination with managers on project staffing, including, but not limited to; recruitment, development, retention, and succession of project staff; development of plan for project staff reporting; and support for performance and compensation reviews.
Partners with Client Service Leaders and pursuit champions to assist with business development, building client relationships, and pursuit efforts for strategic and mini-mega projects in accordance with HNTB's Sophisticated Sales Approach (SSA). Works with the project team and marketing resources to prepare appropriate proposal and presentation materials. Leads proposal development and interview presentations for strategic and mini-mega projects to the client as well as general presentations within the industry and community.
May be responsible for the recruitment, hiring, development, and retention of staff, including development of plan for staff reporting, performance and compensation reviews, and succession.
Performs other duties as assigned.

What You'll Need

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering and 8 years of relevant experience
2 years task management or Deputy PM experience

What You'll Bring

Winning, contracting, and successfully delivering 4for4 (on-time, on-budget, quality, client satisfaction) on smaller projects. Identifying and escalating risk and change management issues, with oversight from more experienced staff.
Leading a team for a smaller project or task order with no or few subconsultants.
Using system tools to manage, monitor, and deliver smaller projects or task orders.
Leveraging the Office Management Team to assist in implementing HNTB Sophisticated processes as applicable to the project.
Interfacing with your client-level peer on a smaller project or task order.
Providing technical guidance to team and task leads as well as performing portions of the technical work. **

What We Prefer

Master’s degree in Engineering
10 years relevant experience
Professional Engineer (PE) certification
American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP) certification
Project Management Professional (PMP)
Local municipal and/or DOT experience and relationships
Active engagement in local professional and/or civic organizations
Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Additional Information

Click here for benefits information: HNTB Total Rewards

Click here to learn more about Equal Opportunity Employer/Disability/Veteran

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

\#EL #Water

Locations:

Des Moines, IA, Kansas City, MO, Oklahoma City, OK, Overland Park, KS (129th Street), St. Louis, MO

Notice To Third-party Agencies

HNTB does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or agencies. Any staffing/employment agency, person or entity that submits an unsolicited resume to this site does so with the understanding that the applicant's resume will become the property of HNTB. HNTB will have the right to hire that applicant at its discretion and without any fee owed to the submitting staffing/employment agency, person or entity. Staffing/employment agencies who have fee agreements with HNTB must submit applicants to the designated HNTB recruiter to be eligible for placement fees.

jobs.description:
Advertisement Closes

11/12/2026 (11:59 PM ET)

2605835

Environmental Scientist III

Pay Grade 15

Salary

$4,297.66 - $6,060.44 Monthly

Employment Type

EXECUTIVE BRANCH | FULL TIME | ELIGIBLE FOR OVERTIME PAY | 18A | 37.5 HR/WK

Click here for more details on state employment.

Hiring Agency

Energy & Environment Cabinet | Dept for Environmental Protection

Location

300 Sower Boulevard

Frankfort, KY 40601 USA

Description

The agency may authorize the selected candidate to telecommute. The agency may terminate or modify the telecommuting arrangement at any time.

The mission of the Kentucky Energy & Environment Cabinet (EEC) is to improve the quality of life for all Kentuckians by protecting our land, air, and water resources by utilizing our natural resources in an environmentally conscientious manner. We do this by helping families connect with nature and preserving the Commonwealth’s natural heritage; and by supporting innovative, resilient, and sustainable energy solutions that together bring economic benefit to the commonwealth.

If you are looking for a positive work environment and a career where you can make a difference in the environment we live in, then EEC is the cabinet for you. For more information on what our cabinet has to offer, check out our YouTube page: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCWSuC43XqlHchYeQ66tP7tg and our Careers page: https://eec.ky.gov/Pages/careers.aspx

By joining the Division of Waste Management, Superfund Branch, State Section as an Environmental Scientist III in Franklin County, you will have the opportunity to assist the public by overseeing and carrying out the investigation, characterization, and cleanup of Coal Combustion Residual (CCR) Superfund sites and a broad variety of other contaminated sites and properties.

Holders of the Environmental Scientist III position will complete tasks such as:

Review corrective action and closure permits for Coal Combustion Residual (CCR) Superfund sites.
Perform geological and environmental reviews of site characterization and corrective action reports for releases at permitted Coal Combustion Residual (CCR) Superfund sites and for a variety of other releases of hazardous substances, pollutants and contaminants.
Perform site inspections, site investigations, and environmental assessments involving the sampling of soil, groundwater, soil gas, and surface water.
Review Brownfield Redevelopment applications, environmental assessments, and management plans.
Provide technical assistance to the public and other government agencies.

Desired candidates possess the following requisite skills or experience applicable to the position:

Experience in natural resources, environmental control, or a related area.
Experience in performing geological reviews of environmental compliance issues, site characterization, and remediation.
Ability to lead a group in the office and in the field in the completion of complex technical projects.

EEC provides opportunities for development and upward movement. There is room to grow your skill set as you build your career. Come join our team and make an impact in the future of Kentucky. We look forward to reviewing your application.

EEC participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. EEC will only use E-Verify once you have accepted a job offer and completed the Form I-9. For more information on E-Verify, or if you believe that EEC has violated its E-Verify responsibilities, please contact Department of Homeland Security (DHS) at 888-897-7781 or https://www.e-verify.gov/ .

Minimum Requirements

EDUCATION:
Graduate of a college or university with a bachelor's degree in a natural, biological or physical science OR Graduate of a college or university with a bachelor's degree including or supplemented by 20 semester hours in a natural, biological or physical science.

EXPERIENCE, TRAINING, OR SKILLS:
Three years of experience in natural resources, environmental control, or a related area.

Substitute EDUCATION for EXPERIENCE:
Graduate study in a natural, biological, or physical science will substitute for the required experience on a year-for-year basis.

Substitute EXPERIENCE for EDUCATION:
Experience in natural resources, environmental control, engineering, or a related area will substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS (AGE, LICENSURE, REGULATION, ETC.):
NONE

Working Conditions

Work is typically performed in an office setting. Incumbents in this class may perform work in the field with frequent travel on a statewide basis. An incumbent in the position may be subject to adverse weather conditions, exposure to snakes and insects, water-borne pathogens, broken glass, rusty metal in streams, and hazards common to operation of electro-fishing equipment, which require the following of safety procedures.

Probationary Period

This job has an initial and promotional probationary period of 6 months, except as provided in KRS 18A.111.

If you have questions about this advertisement, please contact Tabitha Aldridge at tabitha.aldridge@ky.gov or 502-782-6302.

Energy & Environment Cabinet | Dept for Environmental Protection

Location

300 Sower Boulevard

Frankfort, KY 40601 USA

The agency may authorize the selected applicant to telecommute on a hybrid schedule. The agency may terminate or modify the telecommuting arrangement at any time.

Description

The Certification and Licensing Branch (CLB) is home to the solid waste, drinking water and wastewater certification programs. Through education and certification exams, these programs help ensure that the people responsible for managing community solid waste, drinking water and wastewater have the knowledge and skills necessary to perform these important roles.

If you are looking for a positive work environment and a career where you can make a difference in the environment we live in, the Kentucky Operator Certification Program (OCP) within CLB may be the place for you. For more information about the program, visit the Kentucky Operator Certification Program webpage.

By joining the Certification and Licensing Branch as an Environmental Scientist Consultant in Franklin County, you will have the opportunity to serve in an advanced technical role supporting Kentucky’s drinking water, wastewater and solid waste operator certification programs.

This Position Will Complete Tasks Such As

Lead technical reviews of operator certification applications, training requests, scientific documents and program data.
Coordinate and deliver drinking water, wastewater and solid waste certification and continuing education training statewide.
Serve as a technical and scientific resource on certification programs, policies, regulations and examinations.
Coordinate scientific projects, case management activities and technical work involving staff and agency stakeholders.
Conduct and support enforcement activities, including technical review of noncompliance information, site documentation and evidence used in case development.
Provide technical assistance and scientific guidance to certification boards, regulated facilities, government agencies and other stakeholders.
Analyze and maintain program information, develop procedures and prepare technical and program reports.

In This Position You Will Strengthen Skills In

Technical and scientific analysis.
Regulatory interpretation and compliance.
Training development and presentation.
Project and case coordination.
Technical writing and documentation.
Communication with regulated entities, government agencies and other stakeholders.
Leadership and collaboration.

Desired Candidates Possess Skills Or Experience In

Written and verbal communication.
Environmental science or related technical work.
Reviewing and interpreting scientific and technical information.
Problem-solving and sound judgment.
Organization and time management.
Presenting technical information to diverse audiences.
Working independently and as part of a team.

EEC participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. EEC will only use E-Verify once you have accepted a job offer and completed the Form I-9. For more information on E-Verify, or if you believe that EEC has violated its E-Verify responsibilities, please contact Department of Homeland Security (DHS) at 888-897-7781 or https://www.e-verify.gov/ .

EEC provides opportunities for professional development and career growth. This position offers the opportunity to expand your technical expertise while contributing to programs that protect public health and Kentucky’s environment. Come join our team and make an impact on the future of Kentucky.

Minimum Requirements

EDUCATION:
Graduate of a college or university with a bachelor's degree in a natural, biological or physical science OR Graduate of a college or university with a bachelor's degree including or supplemented by 20 semester hours in a natural, biological or physical science.

EXPERIENCE, TRAINING, OR SKILLS:
Eight years of experience in natural resources, environmental control, or a related area.

Substitute EDUCATION for EXPERIENCE:
Graduate study in a natural, biological, or physical science will substitute for the required experience on a year-for-year basis.

Substitute EXPERIENCE for EDUCATION:
Experience in natural resources, environmental control, engineering, or a related area will substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS (AGE, LICENSURE, REGULATION, ETC.):
NONE

Working Conditions

Work is typically performed in an office setting. Incumbents in this class may perform work in the field with frequent travel on a statewide basis.

Probationary Period

This job has an initial and promotional probationary period of 6 months, except as provided in KRS 18A.111.

If you have questions about this advertisement, please contact Veronica Roland at Veronica.Roland@ky.gov or 502-782-6441.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist I
jobs.description:
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST I

Three Notch Group

Company Overview

Three Notch Group is a Top 400 ENR design firm with over 80 years of experience, dedicated to delivering a wide range of services, including Field and Lab Services, UST, Environmental, Utility, Transportation, Geotechnical & Construction Engineering, and Civil/Site Development. We foster a collaborative environment where team members can build lasting friendships, support one another, and guide our clients in shaping their futures. With offices across the Southeast, including seven in Alabama, two in North Carolina, one in Florida, one in Georgia, and one in Tennessee, we offer an exceptional opportunity for personal and professional growth. If you’re ready to make a difference and advance your career, join us at Three Notch and be part of a team that truly values your contributions!

Position Overview

Three Notch Group is seeking an Environmental Scientist I to perform a variety of environmental services and support environmental assessments, reports, and project evaluations. Working under appropriate supervision, this entry-level role will assist with field activities, environmental documentation, project deliverables, client communication, and department standards while developing technical knowledge and professional independence.

The ideal candidate is an early-career environmental professional who is eager to apply academic knowledge to real projects, gain both office and field experience, build strong client and team relationships, and pursue continued professional development.

Primary Responsibilities

Assist with client communication and maintain appropriate contact throughout assigned projects.
Under supervision, perform field work and prepare environmental assessments, reports, evaluations, and other project deliverables.
Assist with scopes and fee proposals for new project opportunities and support project follow-up after completion.
Provide support for department protocols, guidelines, standards, and quality requirements related to environmental work.
Assist with reviewing project plans, specifications, and cost estimates for consistency with project scope and applicable standards.
Monitor task budgets, schedules, field-supply expenses, and reimbursable project costs under the direction of the Project Manager or Practice Leader.
Manage time effectively to complete accurate, quality work within established project schedules and budgets.
Identify opportunities for additional environmental consulting services that may benefit existing clients.
Perform field activities in accordance with company safety policies and established procedures.
Participate in assigned training, professional activities, software development, conferences, certifications, licensure, and other professional-development opportunities.
Maintain required continuing-education units and professional credentials, as applicable.
Follow established guidelines, company policies, and procedures and perform other duties as assigned.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means consistently completing accurate, well-organized environmental field work and technical documentation while meeting assigned quality, schedule, and budget expectations. The Environmental Scientist I will communicate effectively with clients, project leaders, and team members; follow safety and department standards; and demonstrate accountability for assigned office and field responsibilities.

The successful candidate will steadily expand knowledge of environmental regulations, field methods, reporting requirements, project-delivery processes, and client service. They will actively pursue professional development while contributing positively to client satisfaction, teamwork, safety, financial performance, and the continued growth of the Environmental Science practice.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science or a related discipline with zero to two years of experience.
Three months of relevant environmental internship, work, or research experience preferred.
Valid driver’s license required.
Knowledge of environmental regulations.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite or related software.
Strong written and verbal communication, organizational, interpersonal, time-management, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently on assigned tasks and collaboratively with project teams.
Ability to perform essential environmental support duties in both office and field environments.
Ability to sit and work at a computer for extended periods and to stand, walk, bend, stoop, reach, read, write, see, hear, and communicate as required for the role.
Ability to lift 25 pounds or more and work extended hours when needed.
Ability and willingness to work outdoors in varying weather conditions, work around loud project or construction-site environments, and travel overnight occasionally.

Ready to Make an Impact?

If you enjoy combining field work, scientific analysis, client service, and clear technical communication to help solve environmental challenges, we would love to hear from you.

At Three Notch Group, you will have the opportunity to collaborate with talented professionals across multiple disciplines, contribute to meaningful projects, and help clients and communities make informed environmental decisions.

Bring your curiosity, organization, and drive to a team where your work matters. Apply today and help us protect what matters and pursue what’s next at Three Notch Group.

Benefits

Competitive pay based on experience and certifications
Opportunities for advancement and technical training
Company vehicle or mileage reimbursement (if applicable)
Health, dental, and vision insurance
Paid time off and holidays
401(k) with company match

“For more than 80 years, Three Notch Group has been helping clients, communities, and employees build their future. As we continue to grow throughout the Southeast, we’re looking for talented people who want to do meaningful work, grow their careers, and make a lasting impact. We’d love for you to be part of our story.”

– Matt Hames, President & CEO

Three Notch Group, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.

Three Notch Group does not accept unsolicited resumes from headhunters, recruitment agencies or fee-based recruitment services.

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SPECIALIST)

Department Information

California’s Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) brings together the state’s recycling and waste management programs to move the state towards a circular economy that reduces waste and reuses all materials.

Through landmark initiatives like the Integrated Waste Management Act and Beverage Container Recycling and Litter Reduction Act, California works toward a society that uses less, recycles more, and takes resource conservation to higher and higher levels.

CalRecycle’s Mission: Protecting California’s environment and climate for the health and prosperity of future generations through the reduction, reuse and recycling of California resources, environmental education, disaster recovery and the transition from a disposable to a fully circular economy.

CalRecycle values diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. We foster an environment where employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We believe the diversity of our employees is essential to inspiring innovative solutions. Together we further our mission to protect the environment and preserve resources by empowering Californians to reduce, reuse, and recycle. Join CalRecycle to improve the lives of all Californians.

Department Website: http://www.calrecycle.ca.gov

Job Description And Duties

Do you have a passion to perform a variety of scientific, analytical, and technical assistance duties to implement enforcement requirements and assist with program analysis of compliance policies for Product Stewardship Compliance Branch? Do you enjoy working in a collaborative, dynamic environment? CalRecycle is seeking an enthusiastic Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to join our talented team that is passionate to work in the Product Stewardship Compliance programs!

Position Description:

Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager II (Supervisory) (EPM II) in the Product Stewardship Compliance Branch, the Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) will act as a lead technical expert on the product stewardship compliance programs. The incumbent performs difficult, complex, sensitive scientific and technical duties related to CalRecycle’s product stewardship compliance, including environmental and materials management research, analyses, investigations, and enforcement. The incumbent utilizes principles of scientific research, physical and environmental sciences, and statistical analysis, along with expertise in integrated waste management, industry economics, public health, and resource management. Responsibilities include assessing and enforcing regulations, reviewing and analyzing technical documents, evaluating operations and monitoring records, and conducting inspections and compliance assessments. The incumbent is responsible for determining the significance of violations and their general effect on public health, safety, environmental justice, and the environment for the program. Key duties include providing training and mentoring of staff in the determination of compliance with state minimum standards, offering technical expertise on evaluation and enforcement matters; reviewing findings and reports for technical adequacy; and ensuring that enforcement information in the Department’s databases has been accurately input by staff. Additional duties include process development, monitoring, and evaluation to support various functions of the branch. The incumbent will independently identify problems, develop courses of action, and conduct investigations and studies that yield information and recommendations to improve the department’s oversight of product stewardship compliance programs. Additionally, the incumbent will play a key role in the development and implementation of new enforcement programs related to products with extended producer responsibility (EPR) and product stewardship requirements.

This position involves traveling throughout California involving multiple, consecutive days away from the office and overnight stays. The incumbent must have a current California Driver’s License and participate in the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) Employer Pull Notice Program.

This position is required to be in office a minimum of four days per week. This position may be eligible for one day a week telework under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location, as indicated on their duty statement, at their own expense.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

Special Requirements

The position(s) require(s) a valid California Drivers License (CDL). You must answer the questions addressing your CDL on your application. Ensure you provide your CDL number, class, expiration date, and any endorsements and/or restrictions.
When submitting application in hard copy, applicants are required to submit a standard state application (Form Std.678) with an original signature, and clearly indicate HRC0005631 & Position # 835-813-0765-001 in the “Job Title(s)” section of the Standard State Application or you will not be considered for the position.

SROA and Surplus candidates are given priority; therefore, individuals with other eligibility may be considered in the event no SROA or Surplus candidates apply.

Applications will be screened and only the most qualified applicants will be selected to move forward in the selection process. Applicants must meet the Minimum Qualifications stated in the Classification Specification(s).

Application Packages may be submitted electronically through your CalCareer Account at www.CalCareers.ca.gov. When submitting your application in hard copy, a completed copy of the Application Package listing must be included. If you choose to not apply electronically, a hard copy application package may be submitted through an alternative method listed below:

jobs.description:
In a world of possibilities, pursue one with endless opportunities. Imagine Next!

At Parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. Guided by our leadership vision of valuing people, embracing agility, and fostering growth, we cultivate an innovative culture that empowers you to achieve your full potential. Unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible.

Job Description

Parsons is looking for an amazingly talented Environmental Specialist
to join our team supporting our Federal client! In this role you will join a multi-disciplined environmental team providing onsite support at the client office.

What You'll Be Doing

Assist client with executing specific environmental requirements in support of their expanding construction program including:
perform environmental reporting and project planning tasks in support of engineering, planning, and construction teams
conduct detailed environmental analysis of facility master plans, including identifying and assessing environmental impacts of specific projects and activities
Perform desktop environmental reviews of proposed project sites during project planning
assist with appropriate levels of NEPA review for each proposed government action
prepare and/or review programmatic Environmental Assessments and all necessary associated NEPA documentation
contribute to RFP and scopes of work development and review of cost estimates
support Federal client in engaging with the public and stakeholders, including drafting public notices, attending public meetings, and providing assistance with drafting responses to public comments
coordinate and consult with relevant federal, state, and local agencies, including U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS), and State Historic Preservation Office (SHPO).
Conduct site visits to assess federal, state, and local environmental regulatory requirements
Perform reviews of wetland assessments and delineations, threatened and endangered species habitat assessments, and Coastal Zone Management Act consistency determinations.
Review Phase II Environmental Site Assessment and Environmental Site Investigation reports
Review Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans
Assist with responding to environmental-related Requests for Information from construction contractors
Advise client on matters related to compliance with environmental regulations and standards.

What Required Skills You'll Bring

BS Degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Planning or related field
5+ years NEPA and/or Section 106 experience in support of multi-$M Federal client construction programs. (8+ years preferred)
Experience in producing NEPA-related documentation
Ability to manage projects, interface with clients and enjoy being hands on technically in the project.
US Citizenship required

What Desired Skills You'll Bring

Broad knowledge and experience with NEPA/environmental compliance support for Federal facilities and related infrastructure construction projects
Broad knowledge and experience with environmental investigations and cleanup for Federal facilities and related infrastructure construction projects
Deep familiarity with environmental standards, procedures, and approval processes, including U.S. Coast Guard Environmental Planning Implementing Procedures
Certification as PMP with the Project Management Institute (PMI)
Developed soft skills working as part of a team with Federal client
Excellent writing and oral communication skills.
Proven ability for performing in a lead capacity on a project

Security Clearance Requirement

None

This position is part of our Federal Solutions team.

The Federal Solutions segment delivers resources to our US government customers that ensure the success of missions around the globe. Our intelligent employees drive the state of the art as they provide services and solutions in the areas of defense, security, intelligence, infrastructure, and environmental. We promote a culture of excellence and close-knit teams that take pride in delivering, protecting, and sustaining our nation's most critical assets, from Earth to cyberspace. Throughout the company, our people are anticipating what’s next to deliver the solutions our customers need now.

Salary Range: $74,800.00 - $130,900.00

We value our employees and want our employees to take care of their overall wellbeing, which is why we offer best-in-class benefits such as medical, dental, vision, paid time off, Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), 401(k), life insurance, flexible work schedules, and holidays to fit your busy lifestyle!

We truly invest and care about our employee’s wellbeing and provide endless growth opportunities as the sky is the limit, so aim for the stars! Imagine next and join the Parsons quest—APPLY TODAY!

Ability and willingness to work outdoors in varying weather conditions, work around loud project or construction-site environments, and travel overnight occasionally.

If you enjoy combining field work, scientific analysis, client service, and clear technical communication to help solve environmental challenges, we would love to hear from you.

At Three Notch Group, you will have the opportunity to collaborate with talented professionals across multiple disciplines, contribute to meaningful projects, and help clients and communities make informed environmental decisions.

Bring your curiosity, organization, and drive to a team where your work matters. Apply today and help us protect what matters and pursue what’s next at Three Notch Group.

We’d love for you to be part of our story.”

jobs.title: Environmental Health Specialist I/II/III - Community Services
jobs.description:
Description

WHAT WE OFFER

Benefits

The County of Ventura offers an attractive compensation and benefits package. In addition to the salary of approximately $60,368.09 to $111,745.42 annually an employee within this position will also be eligible for the following:

General Salary Increase - 3.5% effective December 20, 2026, and December 19, 2027.
Educational Incentive - An educational incentive of 2.5% for completion of an associate's degree, 3.5% for completion of a bachelor's degree, OR 5% for completion of a graduate's degree.
Bilingual Incentive - Proficiency levels by exam are $.69 per hour (Level I), $1.00 per hour (Level II), or $1.32 per hour (Level Ill).
Sick Leave - Full-time regular employees accrue 3.08 hours of sick leave per pay period with an advance at hire of 40.04 hours which will be balanced at the completion of 13 bi-weekly pay periods.
Vacation Redemption - After 14,560 hours of continuous County service (approximately seven (7) years an employee may elect to receive cash in lieu of up to (80) hours of vacation accrual at current hourly rate of pay/salary rate.
Deferred Compensation - Eligible to participate in the County's 401(k) Shared Savings Plan and/or the Section 457 Plan. This position is eligible for up to a 3% match on your 401(k) contributions.

Health Insurance - Full-time regular employees are provided an annual flexible credit allowance of up to $26,626.96 to help offset the cost of medical insurance for themselves and their eligible dependents.
Employee only - $463.99 per biweekly pay period
Employee plus one dependent - $834.32 per biweekly pay period
Employee plus family - $1,024.11 per biweekly pay period.

Flexible Spending Accounts - Choice of participation in the Flexible Spending Accounts which increase spending power through reimbursement of pre-tax dollars for IRS approved dependent care and health care expenses.
Pension Plan - Both the County and employees contribute to the County's Retirement Plan and to Social Security. If eligible, reciprocity may be established with other public retirement systems, such as CalPERS.
Holidays - 13 paid days per year which includes a scheduled floating holiday.

VENTURA COUNTY

The County's 1,873 square miles include 1,846 square miles of land with 42 miles of coastline which is home to the following cities and points of interest: Camarillo, Fillmore, Moorpark, Ojai, Oxnard, Port Hueneme, Santa Paula, Simi Valley, Thousand Oaks, and Ventura as well as national protected areas such as parts of the Angeles National Forest, Channel Islands National Park, and the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area.

Ventura County is a “general law” county, governed by a five-member, elected-by-district Board of Supervisors. The Supervisors appoint a County Executive Officer (CEO) to oversee the County budget, day-to-day operations, and to advise, assist, and act as an agent for the Board of Supervisors in all matters under the Board’s jurisdiction. It focuses on serving its residents by promoting engagement, strategy, execution and accountability to include diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives to ensure that all employees are treated with respect and without discrimination, and to improve culturally appropriate outcomes for community members.

THE AGENCY

The primary goal of the Resource Management Agency (RMA) is to protect the health, safety and welfare of the general public through administration and enforcement of County ordinances, Board policy, and state and federal laws regarding land use, and commercial and environmental regulation. RMA includes five divisions: Environmental Health, Planning, Building &Safety, Code Compliance, and Operations/GIS.

RMA recognizes the value of having a diverse and inclusive workforce at all levels of our agency to best serve our clients and be representative of the community we serve and is committed to being an active participant in removing barriers to ensure equitable access and opportunities for success. The agency is dedicated to attracting, hiring, developing, retaining and valuing quality employees fully empowered to protect everyone’s health, safety, and the environment, and committed to providing excellent customer service through the efficient, accurate, and consistent application of laws, ordinances, regulations, and policies.

THE DIVISION

The key responsibility of the Environmental Health Division is to protect public health and the environment by ensuring conformance with State laws and County ordinances pertaining to the following programs: food protection, hazardous materials, hazardous waste, individual sewage disposal systems, land use, medical waste, ocean water quality monitoring, recreational health, solid waste, underground fuel tanks, and vector control.

The Position

Under immediate supervision (I), general supervision (II), direction (III), to general direction (IV), performs progressively complex professional environmental health activities involving investigation, inspection, data collection and analysis, enforcement action, report preparation and public contact; assists in environmental health program administration; and performs related duties as required.

Distinguishing Characteristics

There are four levels (I - IV) in the Environmental Health Specialist series. Each level performs increasingly responsible public contact; interaction with public and private entities; conflict resolution; and a wider range of environmental health projects at a higher level of complexity (i.e., understanding concepts relating to environmental, biological, water, wastewater, etc.). Those at the Environmental Health Specialist IV level may act as project team leaders and program coordinators. Each succeeding step in the job series is expected to function at a higher level of individual initiative, creativity, self-direction, and independent judgment.

Approximate Salaries

Environmental Health Specialist I: $29.02 - $40.61 (hourly)

Environmental Health Specialist II: $2,760.32 - $3,854.44 (biweekly)

Environmental Health Specialist III: $3,063.54 - $4,297.90 (biweekly)

Environmental Health Specialist I is represented by the Services Employees' International Union (SEIU) and is eligible for overtime compensation.

Environmental Health Specialist II/III are represented by the Services Employees' International Union (SEIU) and are not eligible for overtime compensation.

NOTE: If appointed at the lower level, incumbent may be promoted to the higher level without further examination upon meeting the minimum requirements, demonstrating satisfactory performance, and in accordance with the business needs of the department.

TENTATIVE SCHEDULE

OPENING DATE:
11/2/2026

CLOSING DATE:
11/23/2026

Examples Of Duties

Duties may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Performs inspections of various facilities and properties, including food facilities, public pools and community events to determine conformance with applicable State laws and County Ordinance Code sections.
Prepares written reports related to food and pool facilities and makes recommendations for completion of environmental health projects.
Researches, compiles, synthesizes, analyzes and interprets information and data necessary to meet environmental health objectives.
Coordinates environmental health projects, defines problems and alternative solutions, and sets objectives.
Provides general information to the public in response to questions about projects, environmental health programs, applicable ordinances, policies and procedures related to the community services, including food facilities, public pools and community events.
Makes oral presentations to public groups and governmental bodies to provide food safety training and explain and clarify environmental health reports and recommendations.
Coordinates and/or negotiates with other individuals, developers, groups, sections, divisions, departments and agencies on various technical or legal aspects of environmental programs, some of which may be controversial or politically sensitive.
Conducts field investigations and complaint investigations of various sites in order to have first-hand knowledge of the location under study.
May participate in enforcement activities which include civil or criminal cases and may involve issuance of citations, report writing, collection of evidence and court appearances.
Performs other duties as required.

Typical Qualifications

These are entrance requirements to the examination process and assure neither continuance in the process nor placement on an eligible list.

EDUCATION, TRAINING, And EXPERIENCE

ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH SPECIALIST I:

Required

Some experience in environmental health which has led to the acquisition of the required knowledge and abilities. The required knowledge and abilities can be obtained by the completion of a bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health Science OR
a related field degree in Environmental Science and
one of the following:

Proof of eligibility letter (ONLY Options IV, or V), as determined by the California Department of Public Health, to take the state license examination for a Registered Environmental Health Specialist
Proof of a bachelor’s degree in environmental health from a program approved by the California Department of Public Health with the ability to obtain a letter of eligibility to take the required state license examination prior to appointment (ONLY Options IV or V accepted). The following is a list of programs approved by the California Department of Public Health:
California State University, Fresno.
California State University, Fullerton
California State University, Northridge
California State University, San Bernardino
San Diego State University-Graduate School of Public Health.

Environmental Health Specialist Ii

Some experience in environmental health which has led to the acquisition of the required knowledge and abilities. The required knowledge and abilities can be obtained by the completion of a bachelor’s degree in environmental health science or a related field and one (1) or more years of progressively responsible environmental health experience AND
possession of the Registration as an Environmental Health Specialist (REHS) in California.

Substitution: A Master's degree in environmental health science or a related field.

Environmental Health Specialist Iii

Considerable experience in environmental health which has led to the acquisition of the required knowledge and abilities. The required knowledge and abilities can be obtained by the completion of a Bachelor degree in environmental health science or a related field and three (3) or more years of progressively responsible environmental health experience AND
possession of the Registration as an Environmental Health Specialist (REHS) in California.

Substitution: A Master's degree in environmental health science or a related field.

Necessary Special Requirements

Must be able to obtain at time of appointment and maintain a valid California driver license.
Candidates appointed as an Environmental Health Specialist I level in Community Services positions are REQUIRED to show proof of registration as an Environmental Health Specialist prior to completion of the probationary period.
Depending on assignment, must be willing to work evenings, weekends, and holidays throughout Ventura County all year long may be required.

DESIRED

Some experience in the Environmental Health field conducting inspections of retail food facilities, public swimming pools, or temporary food facilities, along with enforcement of state laws in these facilities.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Work is performed in an office environment and in the field and may require occasional exposure to hazardous conditions and moderate physical demands while making inspections.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS And ABILITIES

Some to comprehensive (depending on level in series) knowledge of:

Chemistry, microbiology, foodborne illness path

jobs.title: Staff/Services Specialists - Watershed Protection District and Fox Canyon Groundwater Management
jobs.description:
Description

WHAT WE OFFER

Educational Incentive: An educational incentive of 2.5% for completion of an associate degree, 3.5% for completion of a bachelor's degree OR 5% for completion of a graduate degree.
Bilingual Incentive: Proficiency levels by exam are $.69 per hour (Level I); $1.00 per hour (Level II); or $1.32 per hour (Level III).
Vacation Accrual: New regular, full-time employees shall accrue approximately 14 days of vacation a year for the first 10,400 hours or 5 years of service; vacation accruals increase at 5, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 20 years of service topping out at 26 days a year and 400 hours of vacation hours banked.
Vacation Redemption: After 14,560 hours of continuous service an employee may elect to "cash in" or redeem up to 80 hours of vacation accrued in the same year after using 80 hours of vacation in the preceding 12 months.
Sick Leave: Full-time Regular employees accrue 3.08 hours of sick leave per pay period with an advance at hire of 40.04 hours which will be balanced at the completion of 13 bi-weekly pay periods.
Deferred Compensation: Eligible to participate in the County's 401(k) Shared Savings Plan and/or the Section 457 Plan. This position is eligible for up to a 3% match on your 401(k) contributions.
Health Plans: Full-time employees are afforded a flexible credit allowance for purchasing medical, dental, and/or vision insurance from a group of authorized plans: Tier One for employee only is $463.99 per biweekly pay period, Tier Two for employee plus one is $834.32 per biweekly pay period and Tier Three for employee plus family is $1,024.11 per biweekly pay period.
Flexible Spending Accounts: Choice of participation in the Flexible Spending Accounts which increase spending power through reimbursement of pre-tax dollars for IRS approved dependent care and health care expenses.
Pension Plan: Both the County and employees contribute to the County's Retirement Plan and to Social Security. If eligible, reciprocity may be established with other public retirement systems, such as PERS.
Holidays: 13 paid days per year which includes a scheduled floating holiday.

The PUBLIC WORKS AGENCY,
Watershed Protection District
operates and maintains 216 miles of improved channels, 55 dams, 4 coastal pump stations and 148 rain and stream gauges with a $2.7B current replacement value; and is responsible for planning, design (hydrology and hydraulic and structural), and construction of flood conveyance assets, and permitting authority for 950 miles of jurisdictional watercourses. The Department also provides staff to the Fox Canyon Groundwater Management Agency.

THE POSITIONS

Under general direction, supervises a line or operations work unit, performs staff support duties, or acts as a technical resource for mid-level management. Depending on assignment, the incumbent may be involved in planning and supervising the work of clerical or technical support staff, performing special studies, developing and monitoring grants and contracts, and/or at times performing the most complex duties and assignments.

Assignments at the I or II level depend on the relative complexity of the service operation or other work performed, and the impact on other County agencies and departments. Incumbents at the higher level are expected to demonstrate greater initiative, self-direction and independent judgment.

There are currently two (2) Regular Full-time vacancies within the Public Works Agency (PWA), Watershed Protection:

One (1) Staff/Services Specialist I position assigned in Ventura, Fox Canyon Groundwater Management Agency; and
One (1) Staff/Services Specialist I/II position assigned in Ventura, Strategic Resiliency Group.

For the position in the Fox Canyon Groundwater Management Agency (FCGMA),
under general direction of the Executive Officer, the Staff/Services Specialist I serves as a vital professional administrative link between the Board of Directors, District management, staff, and the public. Under general direction, they manage all official proceedings and records of the Board of Directors, ensure strict compliance with California open meeting laws (Ralph M. Brown Act) and the Public Records Act, and administer municipal/district elections and filings. We are seeking a detail-oriented, highly organized professional with exceptional communication skills and a deep understanding of California special district governance.

For the position in the Strategic Resiliency Group (SRG),
under general direction of the PWA Manager, the Staff/Services Specialist I/II supervises and is responsible for stewardship of the business processes utilized by the SRG to advance enterprise-wide lines of efforts that effectively contribute to forward progress on mission-critical flood protection facility project improvements and programs. SRG is responsible for analyzing, developing, reviewing and updating business strategies, processes, practices, means and methods required to ensure that the District policies and programmatic initiatives are successfully implemented. Business processes include but are not limited to the enterprise-wide coordination of the preparation of annual budget documents, grant program administration, management, and reporting, strategic planning and project partnership development, levee certification program support, and special projects, as assigned. The position functions as principal staff support to the SRG Manager in providing business process development, administration and continuous process innovation professional support required to advance effective completion of District priority projects and programmatic initiatives.

THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATES

The successful candidate is a highly skilled professional with a strong foundation in business process analysis and program administration. They possess excellent oral and written communication skills and demonstrate the ability to work independently while exercising sound judgment. A proactive problem solver, they effectively leverage automated systems and applications, including Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). With a keen understanding of organizational operations and strategic objectives, they apply innovation and autonomy to support project and program success. The ideal candidate is adaptable, analytical, and capable of translating complex technical or business information for diverse audiences.

In addition to the broadly stated qualifications above, the ideal candidate for each role should also possess the following:

Fox Canyon Groundwater Management Agency

Knowledge Of

Principles, practices, and legal requirements of California special district operations and governance.
The Ralph M. Brown Act, California Public Records Act, Political Reform Act, and other applicable state and federal statutes.
Modern office methods, procedures, and equipment, including specialized agenda management and electronic records software (e.g., Granicus, Legistar).
Business English usage, spelling, grammar, punctuation, and the formatting of formal legal resolutions, ordinances, and meeting minutes.
Principles of effective public relations, customer service, and professional conflict resolution.

Strategic Resiliency Group

Strong background in business process analysis, implementation, and performance reporting
Knowledge of Agency, and Countywide processes for project and program completion
Demonstrated expertise in grants administration, effective management, and reporting

PAYROLL TITLES AND APPROXIMATE SALARIES

Staff/Services Specialist I: $39.32 - $58.35 /hourly

Staff/Services Specialist II: $42.42 - $62.74 /hourly

EDUCATIONAL/BILINGUAL INCENTIVE

Incumbents may be eligible to receive an educational incentive of either 2.5%, for an associate degree, 3.5%, for a bachelor's degree or 5% for a master's degree that is not required to work in the classification. Incumbents may also be eligible for bilingual incentive pay depending upon operational needs and certification skills.

Examples Of Duties

Depth and breadth of assignments increase at the higher level and may include, but are not limited to the following:

Plans, organizes and supervises the work of technical and/or clerical support staff for the Fox Canyon Groundwater Management Agency or Strategic Resiliency Group, including participating in the selection and evaluation of staff, providing training and employee development, assigning work, evaluating outcomes, determining the most effective use of resources and identifying opportunities for improvement.
Provides liaison with representatives from other agencies/departments. Answers inquiries from other staff, members of the public, vendors and contractors regarding the services provided. Investigates and resolves problems related to the line operation's service or contractor/vendor performance.
Assists management and agency/department fiscal staff in the preparation and administration of the work unit's budget.
Maintains a variety of records and produces management reports using automated systems, manuals and other reference materials.
Performs other related duties as required.

If assigned to the FCGMA

, duties in addition to the above (excluding those listed under the SRG) include:

Board Meeting Administration: Coordinate, prepare, and post meeting agendas and notices in compliance with the Brown Act and statutory deadlines; attend all regular and special Board meetings and closed sessions; take accurate official minutes and track follow-up action items.
Records Management: Act as the custodian of official District records, including resolutions, ordinances, minutes, contracts, deeds, and agreements; maintain comprehensive filing and archiving systems in accordance with state retention guidelines.
Public Information & Compliance: Respond to public records requests (CPRA) and inquiries from constituents, media, and agencies with accuracy and discretion; ensure District compliance with the Political Reform Act (Form 700 Statement of Economic Interests) and Assembly Bill 1234 ethics training requirements.
Elections & Board Relations: Coordinate local consolidated elections with county election officials; manage candidate filing processes, oaths of office, and Board onboarding; coordinate logistics for Board member travel, conferences, and calendar management.
Administrative Support: Draft, proofread, and format official correspondence, proclamations, policies, and administrative reports; assist executive management and support committee meetings as assigned.

If assigned to the SRG

, duties in addition to the above (excluding those listed under the FCGMA) include:

Provides principal business process administrative support to SRG Manager in support of efforts required to ensure the effective coordination of the enterprise-wide preparation of the District’s annual budget documents.
Coordinates preparation and effective implementation of SRG’s annual grants management program work plan required to ensure effective administration of a suite of active grants including submitting timely grant progress reports and reimbursement request invoice packages to the grant funders as required by the terms of the grant agreements.
Serves as the alternate Entity Administrator supporting the SRG Manager as the District’s Designated Entity Administrator for Federal grants under the SAM.gov program.
Prepares various business process documents, (e.g. correspondence, reports, board letters, etc.) required to advance SRG programmatic and/or project initiatives, as assigned.

Job Description

AECOM is actively seeking a creative, Deputy Department Manager, overseeing Environmental Remediation operations along the West Coast. These managers are responsible for overseeing the performance of a group of major programs and/or projects to assure the achievement of internal and client-facing KPIs. The location of this position is based in California, preferably in the LA/Orange/Long Beach area, however we will consider those in San Diego or up North in Oakland/Sacramento areas. The successful candidate will be expected to continue to be involved in and execute billable work.

The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:

Project Delivery:
Drives program performance to meet and/or exceed client satisfaction and KPIs.
Understands and drives business performance and the attainment and exceedance of internal KPIs.
Interacts with business leadership on governance & risk issues to ensure risk management triggers are identified and addressed proactively.
Develops and formulates solutions to client problems/issues.
Participates in project reviews of major program/project dashboards/deep dives to identify issues and improve performance.
Works to drive faster adoption of digital tools.
Actively integrates international Enterprise Capabilities into project delivery to meet business targets and works with business leadership to manage transitions.
Continually develops ideas for program and process improvement.
Is directly engaged and manages high-quality client projects.

People:

Builds, maintains, and facilitates trusting relationships with key contacts across the depth and breadth of three multinational chemical company client organizations.
Serves as a focal point for major issue resolution and provides rapid follow-up to address concerns.
Participates in feedback for Project Managers to assure client satisfaction and long-term growth.
Develops and implements succession plans for the team and advises on the recruiting of key people to serve client needs.

Coaches project managers and team members on understanding business performance and internal KPIs; implements processes with Project Managers.
Evaluates individual performance of project managers within the department.

Works collaboratively with Client Account Manager(s), Practice Area Leaders, and Business Line Leadership to grow profitable backlog and ensure financial success of their respective client program.
Develops budgets that allow for business development portfolio management, tracking & optimizing wins and bookings, and project oversight.
Leads capture strategies for key pursuits and major projects within the department, ensures those strategies yield high capture rates, and grows the business and relevant technical capabilities.

Acts as a point of escalation for project issues and makes recommendations to improve performance. This may include addressing project resourcing gaps, supporting technical issues, resolving invoicing and cash collection challenges, addressing subconsultant and vendor concerns, etc.

Ensures accuracy of Workload Planning Tool output for the department.

Ensures the accuracy of the department’s Salesforce pipeline data and associated Detailed Forecast data and output reports.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and 8 years of experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
Successful candidates will have to pass a background check.
A valid driver's license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy
US citizenship or permanent residency is required. Sponsorship at this time or in the future will not be offered for this role.

Preferred Qualifications:

Master's Degree preferred.
15 years related experience.
California Professional Geologist or Professional Engineer
Exceptional communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to clearly articulate messages to a variety of audiences.
Ability to influence others and move toward a common vision or goal.
Flexible and adaptable; able to work in ambiguous situations.
Resilient and tenacious with a propensity to persevere.
Must be a team player and able to work collaboratively with and through others.
Acute business acumen and understanding of organizational issues and challenges
Strong knowledge and track record in the environmental / remediation business inclusive of risk-based strategic asset management and advocacy in multiple state jurisdictions working for an Environmental Consultant.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist/Project Manager
jobs.description:
Do you like working with different project teams in a fast-paced environment? Are you interested in joining an organization focused on making a positive impact? If so, we’d like to talk with you about growing with us.

EnSafe is seeking a full-time Environmental Scientist/Project Manager to join our team of professionals at our San Diego or Long Beach CA, office.

This position has a requirement to work onsite, at the San Diego or Long Beach, CA office, if needed relocation assistance may be offered to meet this expectation.

What We Are Looking For

An Environmental Scientist with proven experience managing environmental due diligence projects and a strong ability to translate complex findings into clear, defensible Phase I ESA reports. You’ll work with clients across California and beyond, managing projects from site assessment through final reporting while gaining exposure to Phase II investigations, environmental sampling, and emerging areas such as PFAS risk evaluation.

Joining our team means immersing yourself in an environment that nurtures creativity, encourages collaboration at all levels, fosters a supportive culture, and facilitates professional development.

Key responsibilities of this position include

What you will be doing:

Perform and manage Phase I Environmental Site Assessments in accordance with ASTM and applicable regulatory requirements.
Conduct site reconnaissance, historical research, regulatory database review, interviews, and other due diligence activities.
Prepare clear, technically sound Phase I ESA reports and recommendations.
Manage multiple Phase I ESA projects, including scope, schedule, budget, subcontractors, client communication, and deliverables.
Provide technical and peer review of Phase I ESA reports as experience permits.
Support Phase II environmental site investigations and other due diligence activities when warranted.
Plan and conduct environmental sampling activities involving soil, groundwater, soil vapor, indoor air, surface water, or other environmental media.
Prepare work plans, technical memoranda, investigation reports, and proposals.
Communicate findings and environmental risk considerations clearly to clients and project teams.
Coordinate work with junior staff and provide technical guidance and mentoring.
Support environmental compliance projects based on experience and workload, which may include hazardous materials and hazardous waste management, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, EPCRA/Tier II, or related regulatory requirements.
Participate in business development activities, including preparation of scopes, budgets, proposals, and support for existing client relationships.
Travel periodically to project sites throughout California and as needed, elsewhere in the United States.

Minimum Skills And Requirements
