jobs.description:
Job Purpose

As an Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) Specialist, the primary role is to lead and ensure the organization’s compliance with U.S. federal, state, and local environmental, health, and safety regulations and standards, including OSHA and EPA requirements. The employee will act as a subject matter expert, driving the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of EHS programs. The purpose is to safeguard the well-being of employees, visitors, and contractors, minimize workplace risks, reduce environmental impact, and promote a culture of safety and sustainability across the organization.

Duties And Responsibilities

The associate’s primary functions and responsibilities are as follows:

Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of environmental, health, and safety programs in accordance with OSHA, EPA, and state regulations.
Act as the site subject matter expert on EHS compliance, providing strategic guidance and interpretation of regulatory requirements.
Conduct advanced environmental monitoring, analyze and interpret data trends, and prepare comprehensive technical reports with actionable recommendations.
Plan, lead, and execute internal EHS audits, inspections, and compliance assessments; ensure timely closure of corrective and preventive actions.
Design and deliver comprehensive EHS training programs for employees, supervisors, and leadership.
Oversee EHS performance metrics (KPIs), analyze trends, and report findings to management with improvement plans.
Drive a proactive safety culture by ensuring effective implementation of plant safety rules, housekeeping standards, and PPE compliance.
Lead incident investigations, perform root cause analysis, and implement corrective and preventive measures.
Maintain and oversee Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and hazardous materials compliance programs.
Ensure accurate and thorough documentation of all EHS activities, audits, and regulatory records.
Ensure full compliance with OSHA standards, EPA regulations, and applicable federal, state, and local laws.
Serve as a key member of the Fire Safety Team and lead the development and maintenance of fire prevention and emergency response plans.
Lead and coordinate emergency drills, safety inspections, and compliance training initiatives.
Partner with workers’ compensation and HR teams on injury management, return-to-work programs, and regulatory reporting.
Oversee and audit Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) programs and other critical safety procedures.
Lead risk assessments and Job Safety Analyses (JSA) for operations and new processes.
Manage contractor safety programs, including compliance verification, onboarding, and performance monitoring.
Facilitate and co-chair the Joint Health & Safety Committee, driving engagement and continuous improvement.
Respond to complex EHS concerns, regulatory inquiries, and compliance issues.
Support sustainability and environmental initiatives aligned with organizational goals.
Perform other assigned duties
Follow Health and Safety rules and regulations.
Must follow Good Manufacturing Practices, Food Safety, and Food Defense guidelines.
Comply with all Company policies and procedures.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Safety, Environmental/Health Science, Industrial Hygiene, or a related field.
Minimum of 2 years of progressive EHS experience in an industrial or manufacturing environment.
In-depth knowledge of OSHA regulations (29 CFR 1910, 29 CFR 1926), EPA requirements, and applicable state regulations (e.g., Pennsylvania).
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint, with the ability to create and manage documents, spreadsheets, email communications, and presentations effectively.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment.
Professional certification is strongly preferred (e.g., CSP, CHST, or OSHA-authorized trainer credentials).

Working conditions

Always work indoors.
Compliant with ventilation, cleanliness, space, lighting and temperature.

Physical Requirements

Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.
Sitting involved.
May repeat the same movement.
Typing involved.

About The Opportunity

SWCA Environmental Consultants is seeking a Staff Air Quality Specialist
to join our national Air Quality practice. SWCA provides our clients with high-quality air permitting, planning, and modeling services across the country. Qualified candidates will have demonstrated experience in the power generation, oil and gas, and/or industrial sectors.

If you are seeking an opportunity to work in a culture of exceptionally skilled and diverse professionals, then SWCA will be a great fit for you. Our employees are given excellent project opportunities and direct client contact. As a part of the Air Quality team, you will have the ability to make a significant impact in the growth of our Air Quality practice.

This is regular (with benefits) full-time, hourly/non-exempt position that is hybrid and/or distributed (=remote) eligible based out of any SWCA US office location.

To be considered, please attach a letter of interest/cover letter with your application.

Application Deadline
: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and interviews may be scheduled as qualified candidates are identified. This position may close without prior notice once a strong candidate pool is established.

About SWCA

SWCA Environmental Consultants is a 100% employee-owned environmental consulting firm providing full spectrum environmental services across the United States. Our North Star is to be the best place to work and a leader in sustainability, delivering sound science and creative solutions to complex environmental challenges.

We are guided by our core values every day. We collaborate as #OneSWCA, we are #AlwaysLearning, we #NeverSettle, and we #GiveBack to our communities. With offices nationwide, SWCA offers a collaborative, team focused environment where employees can build meaningful and long-term careers.

What you will accomplish

Assists in preparing air permit applications (e.g., NSR, Title V, PBR) for submittal to federal, state, and local regulatory agencies.
Supports air emissions calculations using established engineering methods, emission factors, and operational data for various source types, ensuring accuracy and reliability.
Assists with regulatory research to identify applicable air quality requirements and supports applicability determinations for diverse projects.
Assists with drafting air quality, greenhouse gas, and climate change technical sections for CEQA, NEPA, and FERC environmental documents, demonstrating strong technical writing skills.
Assists development of air dispersion modeling input data and interprets model outputs with guidance from experienced team members, contributing to project analyses. Contributes to health risk assessments and greenhouse gas analyses in support of environmental permitting and impact evaluations.
Supports preparation of emissions inventories and compliance reports, ensuring accuracy, alignment with regulatory formats, and timely submittal to agencies.
Tracks project tasks and deadlines, contributes to internal project coordination, and communicates with clients or agency representatives under direction, maintaining professional standards.
Stays current on relevant air quality regulations and permitting programs, actively applying new knowledge to project work and demonstrating attention to detail, safety, and a proactive approach to problem-solving in a collaborative team environment.
Participates in agency and client meetings, supporting senior staff in technical discussions and documentation follow-up, and maintaining organized project records.
Demonstrates a commitment to safety, quality, and professional communication with team members and with clients or regulatory agencies to support SWCA’s environmental consulting projects.
Follows applicable federal, Tribal, state, local, industry, contractual, and company regulations, standards, and specifications.
Performs related work as assigned.

Additional Job-Specific Responsibilities
[Can Add/Edit Section]

Develop source category-specific emission factors to support air emissions calculations and permitting analyses.
Prepare state agency registrations and supporting application materials required for environmental regulatory submittals.
Review air dispersion modeling analyses for consistency with project requirements, regulatory guidance, and quality standards.
Support client ESG initiatives through development of greenhouse gas monitoring plans and greenhouse gas data management activities.
Collaborate with air quality practitioners across multiple offices to execute air quality projects and share technical expertise.
Contribute to the growth and development of the organization's air quality services through participation in technical initiatives and project support activities.

Minimum Qualifications

Two years of related experience; or any equivalent combination of experience, performance, training, and/or education. Knowledge normally obtained through a bachelor's degree.

Experience And Qualifications For Success

jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Specialist
jobs.description:
The Richland-Stryker Generation project comprises two peaking power plants. The Richland Peaking Plant in Defiance, OH, has six natural gas-fired units with distillate fuel oil (DFO) as a secondary fuel, generating 450 MW total. The Stryker Peaking Plant in Stryker, OH, has one DFO-fired unit generating 19 MW.

Opportunity Summary

The Environmental Compliance Specialist at the Richland-Generation Project is responsible for upholding compliance and environmental excellence within a power plant and regulatory environment. This role implements and sustains environmental compliance programs while providing NERC support to plant management. The position oversees regulatory compliance activities across two facilities, reinforcing high standards of environmental stewardship and adherence to applicable federal, state, and industry regulations.

Your scope of responsibility as Environmental Compliance Specialist includes the following primary functions:

Environmental, NERC & Regulatory Compliance

Coordinate and oversee environmental programs, policies, and procedures to maintain compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, site permits, and other regulatory requirements.
Manage Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS) reporting under Title V permit requirements enforced by the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, including data monitoring, recordkeeping, interpretation, and timely preparation and submission of monthly, quarterly, semiannual, and annual reports.
Develop facility-specific environmental plans that align with regulatory and corporate requirements, ensuring technical accuracy and completeness.
Administer environmental plans by tracking compliance obligations, coordinating updates, and managing revisions through completion.
Oversee environmental programs, including the Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP), Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) Plan, Emergency Episode Standby Plan, Fugitive Greenhouse Gas Monitoring Plan, Operations and Maintenance Plans, and Waste Management Plan.
Coordinate with the owner and environmental regulators on inspections, information requests, permit modifications and renewals, compliance reports, and regulatory correspondence.
Maintain key components of the Environmental Management System (EMS), including the EHS filing system, Obligations Tracking System (OTS), and OSHA- and regulatory-mandated training records.
Ensure plant NERC Reliability procedures and policies remain current and aligned with applicable standards and requirements.

Health, Safety & Risk Management

Safety is a core value at NAES. This position plays a direct role in maintaining a safe work environment and ensuring continued compliance with established procedures and OSHA regulations.
Administer employee and contractor safety programs to maintain compliance and reinforce safe work practices across the site.
Deliver safety training during daily briefings, lead routine site safety meetings, and conduct formal safety orientations and training sessions for contractors and visitors.
Conduct routine site walk-downs to assess housekeeping, identify potential hazards, and reinforce safety expectations through direct engagement with personnel.
Maintain accurate, up-to-date Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) in accordance with regulatory and company requirements.
Investigate workplace incidents, injuries, and near misses by documenting findings, determining root causes, recommending corrective actions, and tracking implementation through resolution.

Working Relationships

The Environmental Compliance Specialist reports to the Plant Manager and maintains a close working relationship with NAES corporate Environmental Support Services and Safety groups as well as Client corporate contacts.

Physical Requirements And Working Conditions

Physical requirements include standing for extended periods of time, climbing stairs and ladders, working from elevated platforms and walkways at varying heights, and routinely lifting up to 50 pounds.

Power plant environment that may involve entering confined spaces, crawling through narrow areas, and handling hazardous materials, with exposure to fumes, extreme temperatures, and noise. Work may include high heat near equipment and varying outdoor weather conditions.

Some duties may require the use of protective equipment, which can include hard hats, safety glasses, and eye protection, air masks/respirators, ear protection, chemical suits, flame-resistant clothing (FRC), hot gloves, high-voltage protective gear, and fall protection. Fit testing for respirators may be required. Strict smoking restrictions apply in and around the facility.

Fitness for Duty

All personnel will participate in the Fitness for Duty Program, which includes a post-offer physical examination, drug screening, and post-employment random drug screening.

Work Schedule

The Environmental Compliance Specialist works a standard Monday to Friday day shift schedule. This position will require extended hours, flexible shifts, weekends, and holidays as needed to support plant operations and business needs and may also require callout availability. Depending on the position, on-call status may or may not apply.

Some travel may be involved to participate in Manager, Owner, User Group, or other offsite meetings.

Compensation

This position offers an annual base salary ranging from $110,000 to $135,000 and includes eligibility for an annual performance bonus.

Environmental Experience & Compliance Qualifications

Associate or Bachelor degree in environmental sciences, compliance, engineering, or related field or equivalent technical training knowledge and experience is desired, but not required. Certification as Level 5 or OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER desired. Relevant industry or military experience may be considered in lieu of education.
Experience supporting environmental compliance at operating facilities is preferred, ideally within a power plant or power-related industry.
Multi-media environmental compliance and safety experience is strongly desired.
Working knowledge of power plant operations, including the interaction between environmental requirements and operations and maintenance functions, is preferred.
General understanding of key environmental regulations related to air, water, hazardous materials, and waste management, with demonstrated proficiency in at least one regulatory area.
Familiarity with continuous emissions monitoring systems (CEMS) software is a plus.
Strong written and analytical skills, with the ability to clearly communicate facts, conclusions, and recommendations in both formal and informal formats.
Effective verbal communication skills, including the ability to serve as a point of contact during regulatory inspections and to deliver training in a clear and practical manner.
Demonstrated interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate and build consensus among internal and external stakeholders.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in an industrial environment and proactively identify and evaluate potential compliance risks.
Must possess a valid, unrestricted U.S. driver’s license and ensure it remains in good standing at all times.

About NAES

NAES Corporation is a leading provider of operations, maintenance, and engineering services for energy facilities. We serve clients across the power generation, oil and gas, and renewable energy sectors throughout North America and internationally, supporting the full life cycle of power generation and other industrial facilities.

NAES is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. Employment decisions are based on merit and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, military status, USERRA-protected status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

jobs.description:
Principal Environmental Specialist

Job #: req38978

Organization: IFC

Sector: Environment

Grade: GH

Term Duration: Open-Ended Staff (OPEN-OP)

Recruitment Type: International Recruitment

Location: Washington, DC,United States

Required Language(s): English

Preferred Language(s): Spanish, Portuguese

Closing Date: 11/5/2026 (MM/DD/YYYY) at 11:59pm UTC

Description

At the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org

The WBG Chief Risk Officer (CRO) Vice Presidency is the core unit responsible for Group-wide institutional risk oversight, including establishment and monitoring adherence to risk policies and guidelines and risk assessment and reporting to the Board and executive management. Its mission is to enable and support the WBG to achieve its goals in a financially sustainable manner. The VPU assists management with identifying and managing Group-wide cross-cutting risks, enhancing risk response decisions, reducing financial and operational surprises and losses, seizing opportunities and improving deployment of capital. The WBG CRO Vice Presidency includes the IBRD/IDA, IFC, and MIGA risk teams and covers a wide range of financial and non-financial risks.

To enhance accountability and credibility, the World Bank Group (WBG) has established an independent second line of environmental and social risk oversight within its Chief Risk Officer (CRO) function called CROES. While operational teams at the World Bank, IFC, and MIGA are responsible for designing and implementing projects in accordance with E&S policies, the newly formed E&S Risk Department—led by the WBG Global Director for Environment and Social Risk—oversees, monitors, and evaluates E&S risk and performance.

CROES seeks a seasoned, dynamic, and motivated Senior Environmental or Social Specialist with strong technical judgment and substantial experience in social risk management. The selected candidate will support independent second-line oversight of operations and portfolios across the World Bank Group, with balanced thematic coverage of environmental and social aspects, such as pollution prevention, labor and working conditions; land acquisition, biodiversity conservation, resettlement and livelihood restoration; stakeholder engagement and grievance mechanisms. The role will identify project-level and systemic social and environmental risks, assess the adequacy of mitigation and implementation arrangements, and provide clear advice to CROES management and senior decision-makers.

Duties And Accountabilities

The Principal E&S Specialist will work in collaboration with the Manager, Lead E&S Risk Specialists, regional teams, and relevant WBG technical specialists. Key duties include:

Independent E&S Risk Oversight

Lead independent second-line review of environmental and social risks in WBG operations, focusing on complex and high-risk projects and material implications for affected communities, the environment, development outcomes, and institutional reputation.
Assess the adequacy of E&S risk identification, assessment, mitigation measures, monitoring arrangements, and escalation pathways proposed by operational teams, while maintaining independence from first-line responsibilities.
Provide independent technical opinions on E&S risk categorization, application of relevant E&S policies and standards, adequacy of mitigation measures, institutional capacity, and implementation readiness.
Review project documentation, E&S assessments and management plans, stakeholder engagement arrangements, advisory products, and relevant legal commitments from an independent E&S risk perspective.

Lead or support quality assurance reviews of selected operations, assessing the quality of E&S due diligence, management of stakeholder impacts, feasibility of mitigation measures, and capacity to meet applicable E&S requirements.

Portfolio Monitoring and Analytics

Lead portfolio-level monitoring and assessment of E&S risks and performance across sectors, regions, and WBG institutions.
Develop and maintain an E&S Risk Watch List highlighting projects with elevated environmental, social, stakeholder, compliance, implementation, reputational, or development outcome risks.
Conduct thematic and sector-specific portfolio reviews to identify systemic E&S risk trends, recurring implementation challenges, and emerging risk patterns.
Analyze E&S risk events and lessons learned to strengthen institutional risk practices and contribute to enterprise-level reporting and integrated risk dashboards for senior management and governance committees.
Recommend improvements to E&S risk management practices based on portfolio experience, independent assessments, and international good practices.
Monitor E&S risks in projects subject to accountability mechanism reviews, CAO or Inspection Panel processes, integrity investigations, significant stakeholder complaints, disputes, or public controversy.
Advise on risk implications of complaints, disputes, compliance findings, and corporate management responses.
Coordinate with operational teams, regional ESG specialists, and other relevant functions to assess the implications of E&S issues for implementation, development outcomes, and WBG reputation.
Support independent reviews and lessons-learned exercises arising from major E&S incidents, disputes, compliance cases, or implementation failures.

Strategic Risk Advice

Advise CROES management and senior leadership on significant E&S risk developments, emerging trends, and implications for WBG operations.
Support escalation of material E&S risks that may affect development outcomes, compliance, institutional reputation, stakeholder confidence, or the sustainability of operations.
Provide independent perspectives during corporate discussions on high-profile operations, complex E&S issues, and proposed responses to significant implementation challenges.
Assess implications of evolving regulatory, policy, environmental, social, and political economy conditions for E&S risks in WBG operations and portfolios.

Knowledge Leadership and Capacity Building

Serve as a trusted senior advisor on E&S risks across the institution and contribute to building CROES capability in independent E&S risk oversight.
Mentor junior staff and provide technical guidance to specialists, associates, and analysts working on E&S risk reviews.
Represent CROES in internal E&S communities of practice, technical working groups, portfolio discussions, and risk review forums.
Promote cross-institutional learning and dissemination of emerging E&S risk insights, lessons learned, and good practices.

Selection Criteria

Master's degree or higher in environmental sciences, social sciences, or a related discipline.
Minimum of fifteen years of relevant professional experience in environmental and social risk assessment, due diligence, supervision, advisory services, or related independent risk oversight functions.
Demonstrated experience assessing, supervising, or advising on complex and high-risk E&S issues in projects in emerging markets and developing economies, including evaluating mitigation measures and implementation capacity.
Strong technical understanding of E&S risk management requirements and practices, including impact assessment, mitigation planning, stakeholder engagement, grievance mechanisms, and monitoring, with the judgment to provide independent challenge and escalate material risks.
Experience managing or overseeing E&S risks in sectors such as transport, energy, water, urban infrastructure, telecommunications, health, education, or other social infrastructure.
Familiarity with World Bank Group operations, guarantees, private sector investments, advisory services, and applicable environmental and social risk management frameworks, as well as accountability mechanisms and compliance review processes, would be highly desirable.

jobs.title: Entry-level Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Woodard & Curran is an employee-owned engineering, science, and operations firm dedicated to clean water, a safe environment, healthy communities, and happy people. We foster an inclusive, collaborative culture that supports professional growth, flexibility, and meaningful work, empowering our employees to make a lasting impact on our clients, communities, and the planet.

We are recruiting for an entry-level scientist to work in our Duluth, Georgia office who can support environmental assessment, compliance, and remediation projects as part of a multi-disciplinary team. Successful candidates will be interested in ecology, wildlife biology, soil science, hydrology, environmental policy, geography, botany, earth sciences, natural resources stewardship, and water resource management. This position would report to and interact with senior scientists, engineers, and project managers, and would be involved with industrial, linear utility, oil and gas, water resources, site remediation, ecological restoration/conservation, and other environmental engineering projects. The right candidate will be professional, courteous, self-motivated, and diligent. The preferred candidate will be flexible team player and should be prepared to travel for up to 2-4 weeks at a time for certain assignments.

Typical field work activities would likely include wetland and waterbody delineations, stream assessments, threatened and endangered species habitat surveys, global positioning system (GPS) data collection, environmental site assessments, environmental sampling (i.e. soil, surface water, ground water, wastewater, etc.), and erosion and sediment control (E&SC) inspections. Typical office duties would include assistance with technical report preparation, preparation of environmental permit applications, desktop analysis of project sites using Geographic Information Systems (GIS), GIS mapping of field-collected scientific data, assistance with development of presentations for technical workshops and conferences, communication with local/state/federal regulatory agencies, and some limited client communications.

Important Responsibilities:

Delineation of wetlands using the appropriate regional supplements to the USACE Wetland Delineation Manual
Identification of ephemeral, intermittent, and perennial streams
Completion of biological assessments such as aquatic and terrestrial habitat field surveys
GPS/GIS data management and mapping of environmental resources
Assistance with preparation of USACE Section 404 permit applications
Assistance with preparation of State 401 Water Quality Certification applications (including Georgia EPD state waters buffer variances)
Assistance with preparation of NPDES construction stormwater permit applications
Completion of E&SC inspections on active construction sites
Environmental sampling while following appropriate sample integrity and chain-of-custody procedures
Sample coordination with appropriate laboratory for sample analysis
Site visits to document other environmental compliance and associated reporting

Skills and Qualifications:

BS degree in natural resources, ecology, environmental science, fisheries, wildlife biology, chemistry, geology, environmental engineering, or related discipline
MS degree is preferred, but not required
1-2 years of field experience in the ecological and natural sciences is preferred, but not required
Knowledge of eastern United States flora and fauna, especially wetland and riparian flora
Formal wetland delineation training is preferred, but not required
Proficiency with GPS hardware and software (EOS Arrow, Trimble, Garmin, Bad Elf, etc.)
GIS experience (ESRI ArcGIS Field Maps, ArcPro, ArcMap, etc) is highly desirable, but not required
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification is preferred, but not required
Ability to work long, physically demanding hours in a variety of weather conditions in remote locations
Ability to traverse uneven terrain and carry field equipment (up to 40 lbs)
Advanced written and verbal communication skills
Willingness to travel as project requires
We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas for this job opening .

jobs.description:
### **Company Description**

**Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!**

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

### **Job Description**

We have an opening for an **Environmental Analyst** to support the Environment, Safety & Health (ESH) Directorate, Waste and Air Quality Office. You will provide advanced environmental regulatory compliance support in air quality to LLNL programs as well as support to the Environmental Functional Area (EFA) and ESH field Teams.

*Depending on your assignment, this position may offer a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You may have the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week.*

This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level.

**You will**

* Serve as a primary technical contact for the EPA, California Air Resources Board (CARB), and local Air Districts.
* Interpret complex air compliance regulations and legislation, negotiate the best compliance solution with regulators, prepare detailed air permit applications and permit related documents, and serve as a resource for and/or collaborate with LLNL stakeholders.
* Analyze, interpret, and provide guidance on proposed federal, state, and local complex environmental regulations and DOE Orders as they may relate to LLNL operations.
* Conduct complex environmental analyses and audits of operations and facilities to identify potential environmental issues and recommend solutions.
* Coordinate and participate in regulatory inspections, audits, and site verifications by internal and external agencies.
* Perform data analysis including statistical analysis of environmental data; maintain spreadsheets.
* Review air dispersion modeling and human health risk assessment modeling analyses as needed.
* Work independently and in a team environment with minimal direction depending on assigned tasks.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Additional job responsibilities, at the TSS.4 level**

* Serve as a primary technical contact for environmental air regulatory compliance and interpret highly complex environmental regulations and legislation, negotiate the best compliance solution with regulators, prepare detailed applications and permit related documents and serve as a resource and/or collaborate with LLNL programs.
* Analyze proposed federal, state, and local highly complex environmental regulations and DOE requirements on orders for legal and potential impacts to LLNL operations.
* Conduct highly complex environmental analyses and audits of operations and facilities to identify potential environmental issues and recommend solutions.
* Mentor and train junior staff in technical skills, knowledge, and abilities.

### **Qualifications**

* Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship.
* Bachelor’s degree or higher in Physical, Chemical, Biological, Atmospheric, or Environmental Sciences, Engineering or related field, or equivalent combination of education and related experience.
* Significant knowledge and experience in federal, state, and local air regulations.
* Experience analyzing, interpreting, and assessing compliance of complex environmental regulations and recommending solutions.
* Advanced experience conducting audits and compliance inspections.
* Advanced verbal and written communication skills necessary to effectively present, explain and communicate complex technical information to all levels of personnel and management; ability to handle sensitive and confidential issues with tact, discretion, and mature judgment.
* Analytical, decision-making, and problem-solving skills to evaluate, interpret, negotiate, recommend, and implement actions/solutions for complex problems which may involve data and modeling analysis.
* Effective organizational skills with detail orientation necessary to handle multiple complex tasks in a demanding environment with conflicting priorities, tight and changing deadlines, and frequent interruptions while providing high-level customer service, and good follow-through.

**Additional qualifications at the TSS.4 level**

* Highly advanced knowledge and substantial experience in air compliance programs.
* Highly advanced experience analyzing, interpreting, and assessing compliance with highly complex environmental regulations and recommending and implementing solutions.
* Experience mentoring and training junior staff on relevant skills, knowledge, and abilities.

**Qualifications We Desire**

* Master’s degree in engineering, environmental science, or related field.
* Experience with Bay Area Air Quality Management and/or San Joaquin Valley Air Pollution Control District regulations.
* Experience with the management of air quality instrumentation/networks including installation, maintenance, and trouble shooting.
* Knowledge and experience with other relating environmental regulatory and compliance requirements, including NEPA, CEQA, hazardous waste, stormwater, drinking water at the state and federal levels.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you interested in a meaningful and impactful career? Would you like to contribute to protecting people and the environment and accelerating a statewide transition to sustainable pest management? The Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) could be the place for you!
  
  
Are you looking to join a dynamic team and work on a variety of projects to help protect human health and the environment? The California Department of Pesticide Regulation’s (DPR) Worker Health and Safety (WHS) Branch is looking for a Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisor) for the Worker Protection Program (WPP). WPP develops, implements, and evaluates California's pesticide safety regulations for workers, which are intended to provide protections for pesticide handlers and agricultural fieldworkers from pesticide-related exposure. Additionally, WPP develops and disseminates pesticide safety materials and provides outreach and education on pesticide safety to farmworker communities throughout the state. Further, WPP assists with development of mitigation strategies to reduce unacceptable exposures and hazards associated with pesticide use in order to protect workers and the public.
  
  
Under general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I, the incumbent performs a full range of tasks focused on evaluation to assess public health and environmental impacts of pesticide use, development of safety regulations to protect workers from potential risks due to pesticide exposure (inhalation from ambient air, dermal, or dietary from food and drinking water), and development and delivery of outreach and education materials designed to increase the awareness of pesticide worker safety issues and concerns based on practical and enforceable measures intended to protect farmworkers from workplace pesticide exposure, as well as to protect family members from exposure to residual pesticides.
  
  
Duties include but are not limited to supervising, analyzing, and evaluating staff duties; developing work objectives and performance goals, setting priorities, and establishing timetables for accomplishing staff assignments; and making recommendations for increased protection of workers and persons near pesticide applications; assisting in the development of worker protection strategies and pesticide safety outreach and training projects; communicating with worker advocate group scientists, industry scientists, County Agricultural Commissioner staff, other governmental agency scientists, and the interested public regarding increased protections for workers and persons near pesticide applications; and developing and presenting outreach and educational materials focused on reducing agricultural workers’ exposure to pesticides.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Using a computer up to 8 hours per day • Working in a high rise building • Ability to lift up to 20 pounds • Occasional statewide travel with occasional overnight stays. • Exposure to pesticides or pesticide treated areas may be possible and appropriate personal protective equipment must be worn.
  
  
**NOTE:** This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location, as indicated on their duty statement, at their own expense.

**Job Summary**

The Energy and Security Group seeks a Hydrologist / Water Resources Engineer for an upcoming assignment for commercial shale and tight oil and gas development in South Asia.

**Responsibilities**

* Map surface water and groundwater availability, quality and competing uses for pilot and candidate development areas.
* Quantify pilot and development water demand under alternative completion designs.
* Assess floodwater capture and storage, brackish groundwater, treated effluent and produced-water reuse.
* Develop water sourcing strategy: source mix, conveyance and storage, seasonal logic and recycling targets, with costs for the financial model.
* Design groundwater baseline monitoring and assess abstraction and contamination pathways for the ESIA.

**Qualifications**

* Master's degree in hydrogeology, water resources engineering, or related field.
* 12+ years in water resource assessment, including water sourcing for oil and gas or unconventional operations.

jobs.title: Water Resources Section Head
jobs.description:
Job Description

Johnson, Mirmiran & Thompson is a dynamic, 100% employee-owned consulting firm with more than 2,800 professionals, providing a full range of multidisciplinary engineering, architecture, information technology, and related services to public agencies and private clients throughout the United States. JMT is currently ranked #45 on Engineering News-Record’s list of the Top 500 Design Firms.

JMT is an employee-owned firm where people work together, support one another, and take pride in delivering meaningful results for our clients and communities. Our collaborative culture brings together the accountability of ownership, the technical depth of a multidisciplinary team, and the shared commitment to help our people and projects succeed.

What You Will Help Us Build:
If you are a Senior Water Resources leader who enjoys developing people, shaping team culture, and helping a practice grow with purpose, this role offers an opportunity to make a visible impact. JMT is expanding its Water Resources leadership capacity across Texas and Colorado, and we are looking for a leader who can strengthen operations, mentor technical staff, support project delivery, and help position the practice for continued regional growth.

Why JMT:
At JMT, you will join an employee-owned firm where technical leadership, collaboration, and accountability are part of how we work. Our Water Resources practice is delivering a growing portfolio of transportation, municipal, drainage, floodplain, stormwater, and water quality projects, and we are looking for someone who wants to help guide that work while investing in the people behind it. This is a strong fit for a leader who values trust, mentorship, client service, and the chance to help build something lasting in key regional markets.

Position summary:
The Water Resources Section Head will lead staff, operations, client engagement, and delivery oversight for a growing regional practice. This position is responsible for developing people, managing workload and financial performance, supporting business development, and providing senior technical guidance across drainage, stormwater, floodplain, H&H, and water quality services.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Lead, mentor, and develop Water Resources staff, including performance management, staffing needs, and career growth
Manage section operations, including workload planning, utilization, budgets, backlog, staffing forecasts, and financial performance
Support strategic growth planning for the Water Resources practice in coordination with regional and office leadership
Strengthen client relationships and support business development with transportation, municipal, county, flood control, and stormwater clients
Lead or support pursuit strategy, proposals, interviews, and client presentations
Provide senior technical leadership and quality oversight for drainage, hydrologic and hydraulic, stormwater, floodplain, and water quality projects
Advise project managers and technical staff on complex delivery, risk management, staffing, and client-service decisions
Promote collaboration across offices and disciplines to deliver consistent, high-quality solutions

Nonessential Functions And Responsibilities

Perform other related duties as assigned

Required Skills

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, water resources engineering, or a related field from an accredited program
Texas Professional Engineer license or the ability to obtain licensure within 6 months of hire
10+ years of progressively responsible water resources experience
Experience in TxDOT drainage design for TxDOT transportation projects (or other DOTs)
Familiar with TxDOT Design Standards and the TxDOT Drainage Manual
Experience with Open Roads Designer production and Open Roads Drainage and Utilities modeling
Experience with HEC-RAS 1D and 2D roadway drainage applications and stormwater management design
Experience in HEC-HMS software
Demonstrated experience leading, supervising, mentoring, or developing technical staff
Experience managing operations, project delivery, financial performance, workload planning, and client expectations
Experience with business development, proposal development, client coordination, and pursuit strategy
Strong leadership, communication, organizational, and decision-making skills

Qualifications Preferred

Experience as responsible drainage task lead for complex H&H schematic and PS&E projects involving modeling, design, and drainage reports
Established client relationships in Texas, Colorado, or similar regional markets
2-D HEC-RAS, SWMM, ARC-GIS experience
Experience with TxDOT, municipal, county, flood control, transportation, or stormwater clients
Technical background in drainage design, H&H modeling, floodplain studies, stormwater management, and water quality compliance
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams across multiple offices or regions
Certified Floodplain Manager certification or other relevant technical certification

Working Conditions

Work is performed within a general office environment. Work is generally sedentary in nature, but may require occasional standing and walking. Lighting and temperature are adequate and there are no hazardous or unpleasant conditions caused by noise, dust, etc. within the office environment.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by state or federal law.
